title: GENERATION, not SELECTION: induced ARC world-model engines scored on never-fitted transitions clear the recall-style gates only by memorising a 1-4 row tail, and 0 of 15 survive on 120 fresh rows where a perfect stateless engine provably exists
inference_substrate_note: No LLM was invoked and no GPU was used. This scores ALREADY-SAVED engine SOURCE against transitions produced by the offline arcade. GGUF strings appearing in the cited upstream corpora name the generator that WROTE those engines on 2026-08-01; nothing here re-ran it.
solve_provenance_note: No episode was played, no level was solved, no ARC game scored or online was touched. This is an offline measurement over saved engine text; it makes no solve claim of any kind, so the live_agent_self_discovery / outer_loop_re distinction does not arise.
verifier_is_oracle_note: The quantities scored are the project's own shipped world-model trust gates, not an executable oracle that defines correctness. The `__control_oracle__` row IS a lookup oracle, but it is used as a CEILING and an instrument check, never as a result.

model_specs.why_a_model_spec_is_declared_anyway: the artifact is compute-bound on ENGINE EXECUTION, not on inference, but the objects being scored are the OUTPUT of a specific generator and that provenance is the methodology. Naming it is what makes the census re-runnable against the same population.

question: Are the induced engines the live gate rejects NEAR-MISSES (a SELECTION problem, fixable by calibration) or GARBAGE (a GENERATION wall)?
no_p_value_by_design: Pre-registered as a CENSUS: no treatment, no pairing, no arm, so no significance test is defined and none is reported. The pre-stated inferential device is the rule of three -- a 95% one-sided upper bound on a rate when zero events are observed. Every such bound below was computed from that formula, stated in advance.

the_uniformly_zero_finding.what_it_said: its pre-registered primary, HELD-OUT EXACT-FULL-GRID ACCURACY, was exactly 0.0 in both arms on all 168 cells.
the_uniformly_zero_finding.this_run: REPRODUCED IN SUBSTANCE, REFINED IN DETAIL, AND ITS TWO STATED CONFOUNDS RULED OUT.
the_uniformly_zero_finding.detail: exp6018 ran the RETIRED Qwen3.5-9B-MTP generator and derived held-out as `full \ shown`, which commit 253e1b60ed can drive to EMPTY -- both confounds are named in results/arc_object_perception_ab_change_fidelity_20260801/run_ab.py.frozen. This run uses the CURRENT gemma-4-31B-it-qat engines and three EXPLICIT non-empty splits, so neither confound applies. The de-inflated exact quantity (change_accuracy: whole grid right, restricted to grid-CHANGING rows) is 0.0000 at the median, q1, q3 AND at the per-game MAXIMUM for 19 of the 20 rostered games on the gate-faithful split. exp6018's zero was not an artifact of its retired generator or its fragile split.
the_uniformly_zero_finding.where_it_is_REFINED: 'uniformly 0.0' is too strong for RAW exact accuracy, which is not uniformly zero -- it reaches 1.0. But that is NO-OP INFLATION: an identity engine is 'correct' whenever the grid does not change. Restricted to changing rows the zero returns and is near-total.

stateless_ceiling.why_this_is_a_result_and_not_only_a_cont: engines are functions of (grid, action, data) carrying no state between calls, so the BAYES-OPTIMAL STATELESS PREDICTOR -- for each (grid, action) return the MODAL next_grid -- is a hard CEILING for the entire engine class. Where it is 1.0, a perfect engine of this shape provably exists over exactly those rows, and a low score there CANNOT be excused as distribution shift.
stateless_ceiling.self_correction_recorded: the FIRST version of this control was a last-write-wins lookup, and it was WRONG: real lp85 engines scored 0.717 against a 0.25 'oracle'. The control caught itself -- an engine exceeding its own ceiling is impossible -- and it was replaced with the modal predictor. Recorded rather than quietly fixed.
stateless_ceiling.second_self_correction_recorded: change_gate_decision returns passed=True with reason `gate_disabled` when the gate is off, which is the shipped default. The first pass read that field directly and reported 267 of 267 engines passing the change gate. Corrected to change_gate_decision(vr, enabled=True), which asks what the gate WOULD decide.

EXISTENCE_PROOF_tn36.what: the generator DOES produce a perfect, generalising world model -- reproducibly -- on one game. This is why the verdict is GENERATION-on-these-games and not 'the task is impossible' or 'the metric is broken'.
EXISTENCE_PROOF_tn36.reading: 6 of 8 best-of-N candidates score change_accuracy = 1.0000 with precision 1.0000 on BOTH a row-by-row-proven 17-row held-out split AND 120 independently collected transitions. That is not a near-miss and not memorisation: it is a correct world model, written by the same generator, on the same prompt shape, 6 times out of 8.
EXISTENCE_PROOF_tn36.and_it_is_the_ONLY_one: across 3 splits, 4 corpora and 23 games, engines clearing the de-inflated change_accuracy>=0.5 come from exactly ONE game.

CORRECTION_the_zero_is_NOT_uniform_on_th.what_the_first_version_said: that the best engine 'never predicts one whole changing grid', generalised from the 1-4 row gate-faithful tail.
CORRECTION_the_zero_is_NOT_uniform_on_th.what_the_120_row_split_actually_shows: on the large split that is FALSE as a blanket statement. Several games have a best engine with change_accuracy strictly between 0 and 0.5 -- engines capture a real FRACTION of the dynamics. The correct claim is about the THRESHOLD and the CEILING, not about zero.
CORRECTION_the_zero_is_NOT_uniform_on_th.why_it_is_still_a_generation_wall: the shipped threshold is 0.5 (and 1.0 at the refinement loop), the measured stateless CEILING is 1.0 on most of these games, and the best non-tn36 engine reaches 0.2833. Capturing a quarter of the transitions is real and is not nothing -- it is simply nowhere near either the gate or the achievable.

headline: GENERATION, not selection -- and tn36 proves it is about the GAMES, not the method. The generator writes a PERFECT world model for tn36 reproducibly: 6 of 8 best-of-N candidates score change_accuracy 1.0000 at precision 1.0000 on BOTH a row-by-row-proven 17-row held-out split AND 120 independently collected transitions. Across 3 splits, 4 corpora and 23 games, engines clearing the de-inflated change_accuracy>=0.5 come from that ONE game. On the split the live gate actually scores, 2 of 250 distinct engines clear it and the shipped hidden-state trust gate is cleared by 0 of 250 (max 0.4843 vs a 0.5 threshold; 95% upper bound on the clear-rate 0.01191). The recall-style metrics DO show mass -- 61 of 250 clear cell_recall>=0.5 over 13 games, 15 at precision>=0.9 -- but 0 of those 15 survive on 120 fresh rows, where their change_accuracy is 0.0000 and where on 4 of their 5 games a stateless engine could provably score 1.0. On the ACTUAL live rejection set the margins are lower still: 0 of 22 hidden-state attempts reach 0.5 (max 0.1781; 16 of 22 fail nondegeneracy at ANY threshold) and 0 of 28 plain attempts reach cell_recall 0.5 (max 0.2474). Non-tn36 engines do capture a real FRACTION of the dynamics on a large split -- best 0.2833 -- but against a 0.5 threshold and a measured ceiling of 1.0. The gate is not discarding usable world models; the generator is not producing them.

interpretation.the_sharpest_single_fact: the same generator, the same prompt shape and the same gate produce a PERFECT world model on tn36 six times out of eight, and never once produce an engine clearing the de-inflated threshold on any of the other 22 games. The bottleneck is not the gate, not the metric and not the prompt -- it is that the generator can express these games' dynamics in a short Python function for tn36 and cannot for the rest.
interpretation.what_that_means_operationally: prompt-level work on the induce tier -- win-transition supply, object perception, re-ask-on-inert, further threshold calibration -- has no channel to a behavioural metric on 22 of 23 games until the generator produces engines that are right about WHOLE transitions. That redirect is what this run buys.
interpretation.the_SEPARATE_and_real_finding_that_is_NO: the exact-match gate IS mis-specified, and that deserves saying plainly rather than burying: it scores ls20__r0__on -- cell_recall 0.9615 at precision 1.0000, 150 changed cells correct and ZERO spurious writes -- identically to `return grid`. Both get 0.0000. A metric that cannot separate those is not measuring model quality. But fixing it is not the lever, for three independent reasons: (1) the live engines do not reach even the RELAXED threshold (0 of 28 at cell_recall>=0.5, max 0.2474); (2) the relaxed metric already shipped as CARNOT_ARC_TRUST_METRIC=cell_recall and already ran as a live arm (llm_on_fix_cellrecall) with 0 plans installed; (3) the engines that clear it do not generalise -- 0 of 15.
interpretation.why_the_recall_style_gates_must_not_simp: on the fresh split, 35 engines across 10 games clear the hidden-state gate's own quantity with substantial denominators (120-7449 changed cells) -- by SCRIBBLING. su15__r0__off scores heldout_change_consistency 1.0000 (162 of 162 changed cells correct) at precision 0.1017. `consistency` is recall over changed cells and is blind to spurious writes, exactly as its own docstring warns. Lowering that threshold admits more scribblers, not more world models -- and the symmetric metric that would catch them is the one that is default-OFF.
interpretation.the_mechanism_behind_the_false_near_miss: the gate-faithful tail carries 1-4 gradable rows. An engine can reach cell_recall 1.0 at precision 1.0 there by fitting those rows, and 15 did. Re-scored on 120 rows from the same games, all 15 collapse and none predicts a whole changing grid. The apparent near-miss population is a small-sample artifact of the split the gate uses, not a reservoir of discarded models.
interpretation.no_op_inflation_confirmed_on_the_proven_: lp85's 6 best-of-N engines score exact accuracy 1.0000 on an 18-row proven held-out split whose n_changing is 0, and sc25's score 0.9286 on a 14-row split with 1 changing row. Both are identity behaviour reading as near-perfect. This is the 2026-06-21 arc_e3_induced_model_quality finding reproducing on a different corpus.
interpretation.what_would_change_this_verdict: an induced engine, on any game other than tn36, with held-out change_accuracy at or above the shipped 0.5 threshold on a split of more than a handful of rows. Across 4 corpora, 3 splits and 23 games that engine does not appear once.

missing_verifier_gaps.gap: no shipped world-model gate separates a high-recall/high-precision partial model from an identity engine at the granularity the planner needs
missing_verifier_gaps.failure_mode: exact-full-grid match scores both at 0.0; changed-cell recall (`cell_recall`, `heldout_change_consistency`) scores a scribbler at 1.0. The symmetric union metric that separates them is default-OFF.
missing_verifier_gaps.missing_discriminator: a per-transition score that is simultaneously precision- and recall-aware AND predicts plannability -- change_fidelity is the first half but was already measured NOT to predict the second (AUC 0.6085, cluster CI contains chance).
missing_verifier_gaps.priority: LOW-for-the-wall, REAL-for-the-metric: this census shows closing it would not move the live path today, because the generator does not reach any threshold.

duration_s_note: 312.6s = the summed per-game wall of the scoring collection over 27 game workers, as recorded by the driver in out/collect.log. Each worker rebuilds that game's progress window by stepping a real offline environment, collects 120 fresh transitions, and then executes every engine against every split; the engine-execution component alone is 30.076s summed over 826 timed engine rows. Artifact assembly itself took 0.011s and is NOT what is reported here.

CORRIGENDUM_2026_08_02_POST_ADVERSARIAL_.status: adversarial review returned holds=true. The verdict GENERATION, NOT SELECTION stands on three independent legs, of which only one is affected. TWO corrections are load-bearing: the rule-of-three was computed at the WRONG CLUSTERING LEVEL, and the stateless-ceiling control does NOT rule out distribution shift.
CORRIGENDUM_2026_08_02_POST_ADVERSARIAL_.never_prune: every original bound and count is left exactly where it was.

G1_rule_of_three_computed_at_the_wrong_l.defect: the pre-registration declares clustering unit = GAME ('engines within a game share a window, a level and a layout and are NOT independent') and then pre-states an ENGINE-level rule of three. Those are inconsistent; the engine-level bound is only valid under an independence the run itself denies.
G1_rule_of_three_computed_at_the_wrong_l.verified: recomputed this session from 1 - 0.05**(1/n); all three clustered bounds reproduce the review's figures exactly.
G1_rule_of_three_computed_at_the_wrong_l.conclusion_survives: yes -- all three clustered bounds still exclude a rate that would explain a 0-of-136 live outcome as sampling luck.
G1_rule_of_three_computed_at_the_wrong_l.what_was_done_RIGHT: the per-game COUNT discipline was followed everywhere (every gate table cell reports 'N engines / M games'). Only the interval was mis-levelled.

G2_withdraw_the_distribution_shift_exclu.withdrawn: 'a MEASURED stateless ceiling of 1.0 rules out distribution shift as the excuse' (decision point #1).
G2_withdraw_the_distribution_shift_exclu.why: the oracle is a modal (grid, action) -> next_grid lookup built FROM the split it is graded on. The harness source says so itself: 'oracle is built per-split: it must see the rows it is graded on, which is exactly why it is an INSTRUMENT CHECK and not a result' (score_worker.py:142). The CODE was honest; the WRITE-UP promoted an instrument check to a result.
G2_withdraw_the_distribution_shift_exclu.what_the_ceiling_DOES_establish: the split is stateless-CONSISTENT -- no (grid, action) key maps to two successors -- so hidden-state non-determinism is ruled out. At 111 distinct keys in 120 rows a lookup table scoring 1.0 exists near-tautologically.
G2_withdraw_the_distribution_shift_exclu.what_it_does_NOT_establish: that a GENERALISING stateless rule exists over that distribution. The review measured ZERO shared state-action keys between C_fresh120 and the induction window on 5 games, i.e. the fresh split is entirely OUT-OF-WINDOW -- which IS distribution shift.
G2_withdraw_the_distribution_shift_exclu.restated_claim: the 0-of-15 collapse is CONFOUNDED with out-of-window shift; split C's PRE-REGISTERED ambiguity therefore STANDS rather than having been resolved.
G2_withdraw_the_distribution_shift_exclu.why_the_verdict_still_holds: A_tail is adjacent-row, in-window and provably held out (0/250 trust, 19 of 20 games at exactly 0.0 change_accuracy), and the LIVE set is 0/22 and 0/28 with 16/22 failing nondegeneracy at any threshold. Neither is exposed to offline distribution shift. And tn36 is a POSITIVE result ON the shifted split, which shift makes stronger, not weaker.
G2_withdraw_the_distribution_shift_exclu.downgraded_phrasing: 'the strongest selection case was tested and KILLED' -> 'tested and NOT RESCUED, on a split that is out-of-window'.

G3_denominator_and_labelling_corrections.parse_failures: '7 of 48 best-of-N candidates are not valid Python' inverts the run's own missing-is-not-zero rule. Only 40 candidates were ever LOADED -- ft09's 8 were dropped on a 2700s budget and never parse-tested. Honest figure: 7 of 40 TESTED (17.5%), with 8 UNTESTED. Confirmed against corpora_scored.statuses (unloadable:SyntaxError 2 + unloadable:IndentationError 5 = 7).
G3_denominator_and_labelling_corrections.corpora_count: '250 distinct saved engine bodies (4 corpora)' is wrong on the corpora count: the 250 A_tail rows are exactly TWO corpora (inert 135 + objperc 115). bestofn and e3store contribute ZERO rows to the primary split.
G3_denominator_and_labelling_corrections.mixed_units: corpora_scored mixes units in one dict: objperc 116 / inert 151 / e3store 27 are ENUMERATED engines, bestofn 58 is SCORED ROWS. Distinct engines actually scored: 115 / 135 / 25 / 33.
G3_denominator_and_labelling_corrections.cell_ids_are_not_unique_keys: both objperc and inert use <game>__r<n>__<arm>, so e.g. TWO different engines are called 'ls20__r0__on'. The mis-specification exemplar must be qualified by corpus to be reproducible. The sha256-keyed dedup was correct; only the reported identifiers are ambiguous.

G4_missingness_is_systematic.finding: all 52 live margins come from exactly TWO arms (llm_on_fix_cellrecall 26 + llm_on_fix_diag 26). The missing 84 are the other four arms.
G4_missingness_is_systematic.consequence: the live bounds describe those two arms, not the 136. Direction is FAVOURABLE: 42 of the 84 come from arms the gate-anatomy artifact already labelled generator-broken.
G4_missingness_is_systematic.verified: recounted this session -- 28 plain records are 14 from each of the two arms; 22 hidden-state records likewise.

G5_A_tail_is_the_split_RULE_not_the_live.correction: 'A_tail is the split the live gate itself scores' conflates rule with corpus. select_trusted_world_model applies _split_prefix_heldout to _active_transitions() (stalled LIVE rows); A_tail applies the same RULE to a curated level-up-straddling window from a WINNING trajectory produced by a hand-registered GameAdapter. Correct phrasing: 'the same split rule the live gate uses, applied to a different and EASIER corpus.'
G5_A_tail_is_the_split_RULE_not_the_live.purity_is_true_but_fragile: under the shipped default k=None a caller that passes the FULL window to induce_prompt leaks 100% of the held-out tail into the prompt. This run is clean only because BOTH scored corpora pre-split. exp6018 -- cited as the prior art being reproduced -- does pass the full window. Any future scoring of an exp6018-shaped corpus against this split is CONTAMINATED.

CORRIGENDUM_2026_08_02_POST_ADVERSARIAL_.G6_tn36_causal_framing_softened: 'tn36 proves it is about the GAMES, not the method' is an n=1 causal claim. The identical data supports 'the method succeeds only where the dynamics fall inside the narrow class this generator can express' -- a statement about the METHOD. Operational consequence unchanged; the headline should report the fact (1 game of 23 clears; 19 of 20 at exactly 0.0) without asserting the direction.
what_did_NOT_change: 0 of 250 A_tail engines clear the hidden-state trust gate; max 0.4843.
LIVE: 0 of 28 plain and 0 of 22 hidden-state clear; 16 of 22 at correct_changed_cells 0.
0 of 15 high-recall high-precision engines survive re-scoring on fresh rows.
tn36 is a genuine existence proof: 6 of 8 candidates at change_accuracy 1.0000, precision 1.0000, on BOTH the proven 17-row split and 120 fresh rows, 6 distinct sha256.
the exact-match gate IS mis-specified (cell_recall 0.9615 at precision 1.0 scores identically to `return grid`), and relaxing it is still not the lever.
35 fresh-split engines clear the hidden-state quantity by SCRIBBLING (consistency 1.0 at precision 0.1017), so the threshold must not simply be lowered.
